context.analysis:
## Overview
This system screens card-not-present payment authorizations for fraud in real-time and provides a case management interface for analysts to review suspicious transactions. It ensures sub-50ms latency at high throughput while maintaining PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and 7-year auditability.

## Key Elements
* Payment Gateway / Core Ledger
* Fraud Analyst
* Card Schemes / Tokenization Provider
* Identity Provider (IdP)
* Notification Service
* API Gateway / Edge Router (Envoy / AWS API Gateway)
* Scoring Engine (Go / Rust)
* Case Management Backend (Node.js / Python)
* Feature Store (Redis / Dragonfly)
* Audit & Transaction Datastore (AWS Aurora PostgreSQL with S3 Object Lock)
* Async Event Bus (AWS EventBridge)
* Model Registry / Rule Storage (AWS S3)
* Frontend Application (React on AWS S3 + CloudFront)
* Background Worker / Model Synchronizer (Go)

## Relationships
* Payment Gateway to API Gateway / Edge Router via gRPC (mTLS)
* API Gateway to Scoring Engine via gRPC
* Scoring Engine to Feature Store via TCP/RESP
* Scoring Engine to Async Event Bus via Async Event
* Async Event Bus to Case Management Backend via Event Push
* Fraud Analyst to Frontend Application via HTTPS
* Frontend Application to API Gateway via HTTPS / WebSockets
* Background Worker to Model Registry via HTTPS

## Technology Stack
* AWS (eu-west-1): Cloud provider hosting all infrastructure within the fixed budget constraints
* Go / Rust: Powers the high-performance Scoring Engine to guarantee sub-50ms P99 latency
* Redis / Dragonfly: Acts as the low-latency Feature Store for real-time velocity lookups
* AWS Aurora PostgreSQL with S3 Object Lock: Provides tamper-evident storage for 7-year audit compliance
* AWS S3 + CloudFront: Hosts the React frontend with minimal operational overhead for a 3-engineer team

## Rationale
The architecture combines a stateless Go/Rust scoring container with an in-memory Redis feature store to achieve sub-50ms P99 latency at 3,000 TPS. Using AWS-managed serverless primitives minimizes operational burden, fitting within the 25,000 EUR monthly budget and supporting a 3-engineer team.

containers.analysis:
## Overview
The system is a real-time card-not-present payment fraud screening platform deployed on AWS to score payment authorizations, manage analyst reviews, and ensure PCI-DSS compliance. It processes 3,000 TPS with sub-50ms P99 latency while maintaining tamper-evident 7-year audit logs within a €25k monthly budget.

## Key Elements
- **Payment Gateway / Client**: External caller initiating payment authorizations.
- **Fraud Analysts**: Human reviewers managing suspicious transactions via UI.
- **AWS ALB**: Ingress load balancer handling gRPC/HTTP/2 traffic.
- **Fraud Scoring Service**: Python/FastAPI container on Amazon ECS Fargate using ONNX Runtime.
- **Case Management API**: ECS Fargate service for analyst review workflows.
- **Amazon ElastiCache (Redis)**: Low-latency feature store and cache.
- **Amazon S3 Model Registry**: S3 bucket for zero-downtime model and rule hot-reloading.
- **Amazon SQS & AWS Lambda**: Asynchronous messaging and audit processor.
- **Amazon S3 Object Lock**: Tamper-evident 7-year audit storage in Compliance Mode.
- **Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL**: Operational data store for case management.
- **AWS Cloud Map**: Lightweight internal service discovery.

## Relationships
- Payment Gateway -> AWS ALB (HTTPS/gRPC)
- AWS ALB -> Fraud Scoring Service (gRPC/HTTP/2 via AWS Cloud Map)
- Fraud Analyst -> CloudFront/React SPA -> API Gateway -> Case Management API (HTTPS/REST)
- Fraud Scoring Service <-> Amazon ElastiCache Redis (TCP/RESP)
- Fraud Scoring Service -> Amazon S3 Model Registry (HTTPS)
- Fraud Scoring Service -> Amazon SQS (HTTPS) -> AWS Lambda -> Amazon S3 Object Lock (HTTPS)
- Case Management API -> Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL (TCP/TLS)

## Technology Stack
- **Compute**: Amazon ECS Fargate (multi-AZ) chosen to minimize operational overhead for a 3-engineer team.
- **Inference**: Python with FastAPI and ONNX Runtime for high-performance <50ms P99 fraud scoring.
- **Storage**: Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL for operational data; Amazon S3 with Object Lock for tamper-evident audit logs.
- **Caching**: Amazon ElastiCache (Redis) for rapid feature retrieval.
- **Messaging**: Amazon SQS and AWS Lambda for zero-ops, asynchronous audit processing.
- **Networking/Discovery**: AWS ALB with gRPC and AWS Cloud Map for low-latency internal routing.

## Rationale
The architecture leverages serverless and managed AWS services (ECS Fargate, SQS, Lambda, S3) to operate reliably with a team of three engineers while strictly respecting the €25k monthly budget. High availability, dual-AZ deployments, fail-open circuit breakers, and decoupled async S3 Object Lock auditing guarantee sub-50ms performance, PCI-DSS compliance, and resilience against outages.

- Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system for mid-size payment processors, screening card-not-present transactions and managing analyst reviews.
- Designed for high throughput, strict auditability, and PCI-DSS compliance under strict budget and team constraints.

## Key Elements
- Payment Gateway / Client
- React SPA (Amazon CloudFront, React)
- AWS Application Load Balancer (AWS ALB) with AWS ACM
- Fraud Scoring Service (Python, FastAPI, ONNX Runtime, Amazon ECS Fargate)

- React SPA -> AWS ALB: Sends analyst management requests [HTTPS/REST]
- AWS ALB -> Fraud Scoring Service: Routes gRPC scoring traffic [gRPC over HTTP/2 via AWS Cloud Map]
- AWS ALB -> Case Management API: Routes REST management traffic [HTTPS/REST via AWS Cloud Map]

## Technology Stack
- AWS: Cloud infrastructure provider in region eu-west-1
- Amazon ECS Fargate: Container orchestration for microservices without server management overhead
- ONNX Runtime: High-performance machine learning inference engine for fast fraud scoring
- Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL: Relational database with encryption for transactional data
- Amazon S3 Object Lock: Tamper-evident storage for 7-year auditability compliance

## Rationale
- Microservices on ECS Fargate with gRPC/HTTP/2 meet the sub-50ms P99 latency requirement at 3,000 req/sec within budget.
- Fully managed AWS services ensure PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and 7-year tamper-evident auditability while remaining maintainable by a three-person engineering team.

Fraud Scoring Service.analysis:
## Overview
The Fraud Scoring Service screens card-not-present payment authorizations in real-time to detect fraud, while enabling analyst reviews. It ensures PCI-DSS compliance and sub-50ms P99 latency within AWS constraints.

## Key Elements
* API Handler Component (Python, FastAPI)
* Feature Aggregator Component (Python, async Redis client)
* Inference Engine Component (C-based ONNX Runtime via Python bindings)
* Rules Evaluator Component (Python, lightweight expression engine)
* Audit Dispatcher Component (Python, boto3)
* Model & Rule Manager Component (Python, background thread/async task)

## Relationships
* API Handler -> Feature Aggregator: Requests user velocity features [In-memory async call]
* API Handler -> Rules Evaluator: Evaluates hard-coded and dynamic business rules [In-memory call]
* API Handler -> Inference Engine: Invokes ONNX model for probabilistic scoring [In-memory C-binding call]
* API Handler -> Audit Dispatcher: Dispatches payload for asynchronous logging [Non-blocking queue]
* Model & Rule Manager -> Amazon S3 Model Registry: Fetches artifacts [HTTPS]
* Model & Rule Manager -> Inference Engine & Rules Evaluator: Updates active models/rules [Thread-safe reference swap]
* Feature Aggregator -> Amazon ElastiCache (Redis): Retrieves user profiling data [TCP/RESP]
* Audit Dispatcher -> Amazon SQS: Publishes tamper-evident audit events [HTTPS]

## Technology Stack
* Python & FastAPI: Powers the API Handler for high-throughput request validation and routing.
* ONNX Runtime: Executes serialized machine learning models in-memory to meet strict sub-50ms latency targets.
* Amazon ECS Fargate: Runs the containerized service within fixed infrastructure budgets.
* Amazon ElastiCache (Redis): Stores low-latency feature states and velocity counters.
* Amazon S3 Model Registry: Stores versioned ML models and JSON rules for zero-downtime hot-reloading.

## Rationale
This architecture uses in-process components and C-based ONNX inference to eliminate network hops and meet the stringent sub-50ms P99 latency requirement. Decoupled asynchronous components and thread-safe hot-swapping ensure zero-downtime updates and strict PCI-DSS data protection within the 25,000 EUR monthly AWS budget.

Case Management API.analysis:
## Overview
[A modular monolith architecture built for the Case Management API container to handle fraud analyst review workflows securely on AWS. It screens payment transactions and manages suspicious cases while meeting strict compliance and budget limits.]

## Key Elements
- API Controller Component (Python, FastAPI)
- Masking & Tokenization Interceptor Component (Python)
- IAM Authorization Component (Python, FastAPI Dependency Injection)
- Case Service Component (Python)
- Audit Logger Component (Python)
- Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL
- Amazon S3 Object Lock
- Amazon SQS

## Relationships
- API Gateway -> API Controller Component: Forwards REST requests [HTTPS/REST]
- API Controller Component -> Masking & Tokenization Interceptor Component: In-process middleware hook [Python native]
- API Controller Component -> IAM Authorization Component: In-process dependency check [Python native]
- Masking & Tokenization Interceptor Component -> Case Service Component: Passes sanitized case data payloads [Python native]
- Case Service Component -> Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL: Reads and writes relational case state [TCP/TLS via SQLAlchemy ORM]
- Case Service Component -> Amazon SQS: Emits case resolution events [HTTPS/SQS API]
- Audit Logger Component -> Amazon S3 Object Lock: Writes tamper-evident audit trails [HTTPS/S3 API]

## Technology Stack
- Python with FastAPI: Provides lightweight, high-performance API routing and dependency injection for a 3-engineer team.
- Amazon ECS Fargate: Runs the modular monolith container without server management overhead.
- Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL: Stores operational case data reliably with robust ACID compliance.
- Amazon S3 Object Lock: Implements write-once-read-many (WORM) storage for 7-year tamper-evident auditability (R-06).
- Amazon SQS: Decouples downstream event publishing for model retraining.

## Rationale
[This modular monolith architecture minimizes operational complexity and infrastructure overhead, allowing a three-engineer team to operate within a 25,000 EUR monthly budget. Furthermore, internal component boundaries and managed AWS services enforce strict PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and 7-year tamper-evident auditability.]

## Overview
This system provides real-time fraud screening for card-not-present payment authorizations and a case management interface for fraud analysts. It ensures sub-50ms P99 decision latencies while maintaining strict PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and 7-year tamper-evident auditability.

## Key Elements
- **Fraud Analysts**: End users reviewing suspicious transactions via the UI.
- **CloudFront / React SPA**: Frontend container hosted on Amazon S3 and distributed via Amazon CloudFront.
- **Fraud Scoring Service**: High-throughput inference container running on Amazon ECS Fargate with Python, FastAPI, and ONNX Runtime.
- **Case Management API**: Backend container on Amazon ECS Fargate managing analyst workflows.
- **Data Stores**: Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL, Amazon S3 Model Registry, Amazon S3 Object Lock, and Amazon ElastiCache (Redis).

- API Gateway -> Fraud Scoring Service / Case Management API: Routes traffic [HTTPS/REST]
- Fraud Scoring Service -> Amazon ElastiCache (Redis): Reads cached profiles [RESP/TCP]
- Fraud Scoring Service -> Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL: Persists audit logs and decisions [PostgreSQL Wire Protocol]

## Technology Stack
- **Compute**: Amazon ECS Fargate for containerized microservices, AWS Lambda for asynchronous tasks, ensuring zero server management for a 3-engineer team.
- **AI/ML Runtime**: ONNX Runtime within FastAPI to execute fraud models in-memory, avoiding Python GIL bottlenecks to meet R-04 performance.
- **Data & Caching**: Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL for structured data and 7-year audit logs; Amazon ElastiCache (Redis) for sub-millisecond feature retrieval.
- **Storage & Compliance**: Amazon S3 with Object Lock for tamper-evident audit trails and static asset hosting via Amazon CloudFront.

## Rationale
The architecture combines serverless and managed AWS services to operate well within the 25,000 EUR monthly budget while supporting a lean 3-engineer team. In-memory ONNX inference and Redis caching guarantee sub-50ms latency at 3,000 TPS to satisfy strict performance and compliance requirements.

Amazon S3 Model Registry.analysis:
## Overview
The Amazon S3 Model Registry container provides immutable storage, secure access control, and atomic versioning for fraud scoring models and rules. It enables zero-downtime hot-reloading for the Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system while maintaining PCI-DSS compliance and 7-year auditability.

## Key Elements
- S3 Bucket & Versioning/Object Lock (Amazon S3)
- S3 Event Notification to SQS Queue (Amazon SQS)
- Access Control & Encryption (AWS IAM & KMS SSE-S3)
- Model Metadata Manifest (`manifest.json`)
- Staging and Production Prefixes (/staged and /production)

## Relationships
- Fraud Scoring Service -> Amazon S3 Model Registry: Polls SQS queue and fetches version-pinned binaries securely via AWS SDK (HTTPS) using IAM roles
- S3 Event Notifications -> SQS Queue: Triggers asynchronous deployment alerts upon new model uploads (HTTPS / S3 API)
- Fraud Scoring Service -> Model Metadata Manifest: Periodically polls `manifest.json` for atomic version synchronization (HTTPS / S3 API)

## Technology Stack
- Amazon S3: Chosen for managed, highly available object storage with zero operational overhead for a 3-engineer team
- Amazon S3 Object Lock & Versioning: Ensures tamper-evident, immutable model storage required for 7-year auditability (R-06)
- Amazon SQS: Decouples deployment notifications to prevent dropped reload signals during ECS Fargate scaling events
- AWS IAM & KMS SSE-S3: Enforces least-privilege access and customer-managed encryption to satisfy PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance
- JSON Manifest & S3 Prefixes: Implements lightweight atomic version pinning and logical staging separation without custom infrastructure

## Rationale
This architecture uses native AWS serverless primitives to maintain high availability and sub-50ms latency without increasing operational complexity for a 3-engineer team. It rigorously enforces PCI-DSS security and 7-year auditability while staying strictly within the 25,000 EUR monthly budget.

Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL.analysis:
## Overview
The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system screens card-not-present payment authorizations for fraud and manages cases for fraud analysts. It runs on AWS in the `eu-west-1` region within a strict 25,000 EUR monthly budget.

## Key Elements
- Fraud Analyst (Person)
- Payment Gateway / Core Ledger, Card Schemes / Tokenization Provider, Identity Provider (IdP), Notification Service (External Systems)
- AWS ALB, Amazon CloudFront, React SPA, Amazon API Gateway (Edge & Frontend)
- Fraud Scoring Service, Case Management API (Amazon ECS Fargate Containers)
- Amazon ElastiCache (Redis), Amazon S3 Model Registry, Amazon SQS, AWS Lambda, Amazon S3 Object Lock, Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL, AWS Cloud Map (Data & Integration Containers)

## Relationships
- Fraud Analyst -> Amazon CloudFront / React SPA: Accesses case management dashboard via `[HTTPS/TLS]`
- API Gateway -> Fraud Scoring Service / Case Management API: Routes authorization and case requests via `[HTTP/2, gRPC]`
- Fraud Scoring Service -> Amazon ElastiCache Redis: Fetches cached card profiles and rules via `[TCP/TLS, Redis Protocol]`
- Case Management API -> Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL: Executes CRUD operations on cases via `[TCP/TLS, PostgreSQL Wire Protocol]`
- Audit Log & Replication Daemon -> Amazon S3 Object Lock: Exports immutable audit logs via `[HTTPS/TLS]`

## Technology Stack
- AWS ECS Fargate: Runs containerized microservices without server management overhead.
- Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL: Provides scalable, managed relational storage for cases and audit data.
- Amazon ElastiCache Redis: Delivers low-latency in-memory data caching for real-time scoring.
- ONNX Runtime: Executes machine learning models with high performance.
- Amazon S3 Object Lock: Ensures tamper-evident, 7-year retention compliance.

## Rationale
This architecture uses serverless and managed AWS services to minimize operational overhead for a three-engineer team. It guarantees high performance, strict PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance, and robust 7-year auditability within budget.

AWS Cloud Map.analysis:
## Overview
The system provides real-time fraud screening for card-not-present payment authorizations and case management for fraud analysts. It ensures sub-50 ms P99 decision latency while maintaining PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and 7-year tamper-evident auditability.

## Key Elements
- Fraud Analyst (Human User)
- AWS Application Load Balancer (ALB) and Amazon API Gateway
- Fraud Scoring Service (Python, FastAPI, ONNX Runtime, Amazon ECS Fargate)
- Case Management API (Amazon ECS Fargate)
- CloudFront / React SPA (Amazon CloudFront, React)
- Amazon ElastiCache (Redis)
- Amazon S3 Model Registry and Amazon S3 Object Lock
- Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL
- AWS Cloud Map (Registry Manager, Health Check Prober, Discovery API & DNS Resolver)
- Amazon SQS and AWS Lambda
- External Systems: Payment Gateway / Core Ledger, Card Schemes / Tokenization Provider, Identity Provider (IdP), Notification Service

## Relationships
- Payment Gateway calls AWS ALB / API Gateway via HTTPS to submit transaction scoring requests.
- Fraud Scoring Service resolves internal endpoints via Amazon Route 53 Private DNS (UDP/TCP Port 53) using AWS Cloud Map.
- ECS Fargate tasks interact with the Registry Manager via AWS SDK for automatic service registration.
- Fraud Analysts access the React SPA via Amazon CloudFront (HTTPS) communicating with the Case Management API.
- Fraud Scoring and Case Management persist transactional data and audit trails in Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL and Amazon S3 Object Lock.

## Technology Stack
- AWS (eu-west-1): Target cloud provider ensuring regional isolation and compliance.
- Python & FastAPI: Powers microservices for rapid synchronous scoring.
- ONNX Runtime: Executes machine learning models with minimal latency.
- Amazon ECS Fargate: Runs containerized services without server management to fit the 3-engineer constraint.
- Amazon Route 53 Private DNS & AWS Cloud Map: Delivers sub-millisecond internal service discovery.
- Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL & S3 Object Lock: Guarantees relational persistence and tamper-evident 7-year audit logs.

## Rationale
The serverless-container architecture (ECS Fargate) minimizes operational overhead for a three-engineer team while easily scaling to meet throughput demands. Native AWS integrations like Route 53 Private DNS and ONNX Runtime guarantee sub-50 ms latencies and strict PCI-DSS compliance within the 25,000 EUR monthly budget.
